title: Bayesian Multiplicity Adjustments
Bayesian Multiplicity Adjustments
text: pd.adjust() asks single quantity, pi.max: upper bound, set data, prior probability direction parameter. claim made holds prior skeptical , , prior odds direction lowered factor pi.max/(1 - pi.max), raises threshold pd c (default 0.975) c*. pi.max used exchangeable parameters, also upper bound expected proportion parameters family given side null value. Since null effects among , judgment many null effects family contain can guide choice. Alternatively, p0 largest prior probability claim family correct, pi.max = p0^(1/m) m tests independent priori, pi.max grows number tests.
code: library(multibayes) draws <- MASS::mvrnorm(4000, mu = c(1, 0.2, 3), Sigma = diag(3)) colnames(draws) <- c("b1", "b2", "b3") res <- pd.adjust(draws = draws, pi.max = 0.7)   # claim a direction when pd.adj >= c (pd >= c*) res plot(res)                                       # posterior probability across the class of priors joint(draws)                                    # simultaneous credible intervals

what: Prior-odds threshold for the Probability of Direction pd — pd.adjust
title: Prior-odds threshold for the Probability of Direction pd — pd.adjust
text: Converts upper bound, set researcher, prior probability either sign parameter threshold pd must reach direction claimed. function accepts either vector pre-computed pd values matrix posterior draws, pd values computed internally. direction-agnostic directional tests supported: direction argument controls pd computed per hypothesis. threshold governed \(\bar{\pi}\) (argument pi.max), upper bound, set researcher data, prior probability direction parameter (either side null.value). Equivalently, one may supply \(\Pr(H_0)\) (argument p0), largest prior probability claim family correct, \(\bar{\pi} = \Pr(H_0)^{1/m}\) recovered parameters independent priori. hypothesis function also reports pd.adj, posterior probability favored (predicted) direction prior class skeptical ; prior side probability 1 - pd.adj, two sum one. direction claimed pd.adj least \(c\), \(pd \ge c^*\).

title: Prior-odds threshold for the Probability of Direction pd — pd.adjust
text: pd Numeric vector direction-agnostic pd values \([0.5, 1]\). pd input every test treated direction-agnostic direction ignored; directional tests, supply draws. Ignored draws supplied. draws Optional matrix data frame posterior draws (columns = parameters). provided, pd values computed automatically draws according direction null.value. p0 Numeric scalar \((0, 1)\). largest prior probability directional claim family correct (\(\Pr(H_0)\)). Supply either pi.max p0, . p0 given, \(\bar{\pi}\) derived, parameters independent priori, \(\bar{\pi} = \Pr(H_0)^{1/m}\). pi.max Numeric scalar \((0, 1)\). upper bound, set researcher data, prior probability direction parameter (either side null.value); claim made holds prior skeptical . pi.max applied exchangeable parameters, also upper bound expected proportion parameters family given side null.value. Since null effects among , judgment many null effects family contain can guide choice. Values 0.5 set 0.5, warning, penalty applied. Supply either pi.max p0, . null.value Numeric scalar vector. null (reference) value posterior evaluated, specified scale posterior. single scalar applies null parameters; vector length ncol(draws) assigns distinct null parameter. Ignored pd supplied directly. Defaults 0. class priors behind threshold defined estimation prior symmetric null value (see Details), holds flat priors priors centred . direction Character vector "greater", "less", "two.sided" (NULL). Specifies testing mode hypothesis: "greater" positive directional test (\(\Pr(\theta > \theta_\text{null})\)), "less" negative directional test (\(\Pr(\theta < \theta_\text{null})\)), "two.sided" direction-agnostic testing (maximum sides). scalar recycled match number parameters; mixed vector allows different modes across hypotheses. Defaults NULL (direction-agnostic parameters). order Logical. TRUE, returned rows ordered decreasing pd (strongest directional evidence first). FALSE (default), rows returned input order, output stays aligned columns draws (elements pd). threshold Numeric scalar \((0.5, 1)\). threshold \(c\) pd without penalty (default 0.975, two-sided per-test \(\alpha = 0.05\)). function reports threshold implied \(c\) pi.max, \(c^* = c\,\bar{\pi} / ((1-\bar{\pi})(1-c) + c\,\bar{\pi})\). alpha Optional numeric scalar \((0, 1)\). convenience parameterization threshold error scale: supplied, two-sided cutoff set \(c = 1 - \alpha/2\) (alpha = 0.05 gives threshold = 0.975), overriding threshold value.

title: Prior-odds threshold for the Probability of Direction pd — pd.adjust
text: object class pd_adjust (data.frame dedicated print.pd_adjust method), one row per hypothesis. Columns: pd (probability direction, compared threshold.adj), pd.adj (posterior probability favored direction prior class skeptical , compared threshold), pi.max, m, direction. order = TRUE rows sorted decreasing pd. draws supplied, output additionally includes median.est (posterior median per parameter) null.value. print method shows \(m\), \(\bar{\pi}\), thresholds \(c\) \(c^*\), columns constant across rows (null.value, direction) header, followed per-test table; columns remain available programmatic access. object also carries, attributes, threshold threshold (\(c\)), adjusted threshold threshold.adj (\(c^*\)), corresponding two-sided per-test Type error rates alpha.nominal (\(2(1-c)\)) alpha.eff (\(2(1-c^*)\)); retrieve , e.g., attr(x, "threshold.adj"). threshold threshold.adj exact function \(c\) \(\bar{\pi}\), reported per-test rate alpha.eff uses identity \(\alpha = 2(1 - c)\), holds null pd approximately uniform \([0.5, 1]\).

title: Prior-odds threshold for the Probability of Direction pd — pd.adjust
text: Following Jeffreys (1938) Westfall et al. (1997), prior odds directional claim family penalized. pi.max penalty number tests; p0, \(\bar{\pi} = \Pr(H_0)^{1/m}\) penalty grows number tests. direction claim chosen data, penalty applied class priors: estimation prior (prior fitted model) reweighted two sides null.value, prior probability direction lies \(1-\bar{\pi}\) \(\bar{\pi}\), claim made posterior probability least \(c\) every prior class reweights prior parameter. equivalent $$pd \ge c^*, \qquad c^* = \frac{c\,\bar{\pi}}{(1-c)(1-\bar{\pi}) + c\,\bar{\pi}},$$ function reports \(c^*\) (threshold.adj). smallest posterior probability reached prior gives favored direction probability \(1 - \bar{\pi}\); prior posterior probability favored direction $$pd_{adj} = \frac{pd\,(1-\bar{\pi})}{pd\,(1-\bar{\pi}) + (1-pd)\,\bar{\pi}},$$ reported pd.adj, \(pd_{adj} \ge c\) \(pd \ge c^*\). posterior used estimation modified. class defined estimation prior symmetric null.value, priors centred , limit, flat priors. Direction-agnostic tests ("two.sided"): pd \(\max\!\big(\Pr(\theta > \theta_\text{null} \mid y),\, \Pr(\theta < \theta_\text{null} \mid y)\big)\) \([0.5, 1]\), claim made favoured direction \(pd \ge c^*\). Directional tests ("greater" "less"): pd posterior mass predicted side, \([0, 1]\), predicted direction claimed \(pd \ge c^*\). Mixed use directional direction-agnostic tests within call supported: element direction handled independently, threshold \(c^*\) applies hypotheses regardless directionality.

code: # From a vector of pd values pd_values <- c(H1 = 0.999, H2 = 0.946, H3 = 0.813, H4 = 0.763, H5 = 0.891, H6 = 0.987) pd.adjust(pd = pd_values, p0 = 0.4) #> Prior-odds threshold for directional claims #>   m = 6, pi.max = 0.8584 #>   c = 0.975, c* = 0.9958 #>   direction = two.sided #>  #>       pd pd.adj #> H1 0.999 0.9940 #> H2 0.946 0.7430 #> H3 0.813 0.4177 #> H4 0.763 0.3469 #> H5 0.891 0.5742 #> H6 0.987 0.9261 #>  #> pd.adj: Pr(favored direction | y) under the prior in the class most skeptical #>         of it; 1 - pd.adj is the probability of the other side under that prior. #>         Below 0.5, the priors in the class disagree on the more probable direction. #> Claim a direction when pd.adj >= 0.975, or equivalently pd >= 0.9958.  # Equivalent call specifying pi.max directly pd.adjust(pd = pd_values, pi.max = 0.4^(1/6)) #> Prior-odds threshold for directional claims #>   m = 6, pi.max = 0.8584 #>   c = 0.975, c* = 0.9958 #>   direction = two.sided #>  #>       pd pd.adj #> H1 0.999 0.9940 #> H2 0.946 0.7430 #> H3 0.813 0.4177 #> H4 0.763 0.3469 #> H5 0.891 0.5742 #> H6 0.987 0.9261 #>  #> pd.adj: Pr(favored direction | y) under the prior in the class most skeptical #>         of it; 1 - pd.adj is the probability of the other side under that prior. #>         Below 0.5, the priors in the class disagree on the more probable direction. #> Claim a direction when pd.adj >= 0.975, or equivalently pd >= 0.9958.  # Simulate draws Sigma <- matrix(0, nrow = 6, ncol = 6); diag(Sigma) <- 1 mu    <- c(1, -0.1, 0.8, 0, 2, 3) draws <- MASS::mvrnorm(n = 4000, mu = mu, Sigma = Sigma) colnames(draws) <- c("H1", "H2", "H3", "H4", "H5", "H6")  # From posterior draws pd.adjust(draws = draws, pi.max = 0.7, null.value = 0) #> Prior-odds threshold for directional claims #>   m = 6, pi.max = 0.7 #>   c = 0.975, c* = 0.9891 #>   null value = 0, direction = two.sided #>  #>    median.est     pd pd.adj #> H1     0.9860 0.8358 0.6856 #> H2    -0.1175 0.5350 0.3302 #> H3     0.7761 0.7822 0.6062 #> H4    -0.0089 0.5030 0.3025 #> H5     1.9500 0.9762 0.9463 #> H6     2.9866 0.9995 0.9988 #>  #> pd.adj: Pr(favored direction | y) under the prior in the class most skeptical #>         of it; 1 - pd.adj is the probability of the other side under that prior. #>         Below 0.5, the priors in the class disagree on the more probable direction. #> Claim a direction when pd.adj >= 0.975, or equivalently pd >= 0.9891.  # Order the rows by strength of evidence pd.adjust(draws = draws, pi.max = 0.7, null.value = 0, order = TRUE) #> Prior-odds threshold for directional claims #>   m = 6, pi.max = 0.7 #>   c = 0.975, c* = 0.9891 #>   null value = 0, direction = two.sided #>  #>    median.est     pd pd.adj #> H6     2.9866 0.9995 0.9988 #> H5     1.9500 0.9762 0.9463 #> H1     0.9860 0.8358 0.6856 #> H3     0.7761 0.7822 0.6062 #> H2    -0.1175 0.5350 0.3302 #> H4    -0.0089 0.5030 0.3025 #>  #> pd.adj: Pr(favored direction | y) under the prior in the class most skeptical #>         of it; 1 - pd.adj is the probability of the other side under that prior. #>         Below 0.5, the priors in the class disagree on the more probable direction. #> Claim a direction when pd.adj >= 0.975, or equivalently pd >= 0.9891.  # Mix of directional and agnostic tests with parameter-specific nulls pd.adjust(draws = draws, pi.max = 0.6, null.value = c(0.2, 0, 0.2, 0, 0.5, 0.5),           direction = c("greater", "two.sided", "greater",           "two.sided", "greater", "greater")) #> Prior-odds threshold for directional claims #>   m = 6, pi.max = 0.6 #>   c = 0.975, c* = 0.9832 #>  #>    median.est null.value     pd pd.adj direction #> H1     0.9860        0.2 0.7820 0.7051   greater #> H2    -0.1175        0.0 0.5350 0.4341 two.sided #> H3     0.7761        0.2 0.7230 0.6350   greater #> H4    -0.0089        0.0 0.5030 0.4029 two.sided #> H5     1.9500        0.5 0.9285 0.8965   greater #> H6     2.9866        0.5 0.9948 0.9921   greater #>  #> pd.adj: Pr(favored direction | y) under the prior in the class most skeptical #>         of it;
